promotionalText: Find a public Preferans table or gather friends with an invite. Choose your convention, agree on the pulka, and settle in for a game.
description:
Play Preferans, also known as Russian Preference, the classic trick-taking card game for three or four players on iPhone and iPad. Find players in the public lobby, gather friends with an invite link or room code, or practice locally against bots.

Browse waiting tables, see the convention, pulka target, players and available seats, then join. Or open your own public table. Everyone confirms Ready before the host starts. For a private game, choose Invite only.

Our conventions are named Vienna, Prague and Berlin. Vienna offers balanced scoring, Prague doubles whists and uses a shared pool, and Berlin uses semi-responsible defense and a hidden talon on all-pass deals. The settings explain the differences before you play.

Bid for a suit or no-trump contract, play misere, or navigate an all-pass deal. Take the talon, choose your two discards, and decide how to defend. Automatic scoring keeps track of each deal and the final results.

AT YOUR TABLE
- Public tables with convention, player-count and match-length filters
- Private rooms with invite links and room codes
- Three players or four players with a rotating dealer
- Short pulka presets and configurable targets
- Return to your existing online game after disconnecting
- Local practice against bots
- Suit contracts, no trump, misere and all-pass play
- Manual discards and open or closed defense
- Deal score breakdowns and final match results
- Six table themes and readable cards for iPhone and iPad

Preferans is a game of skill. There is no real-money betting.
whatsNew: Find players in the new public lobby, browse table settings and take an open seat. Create public or invite-only tables and confirm Ready before the first deal. Our conventions now use the names Vienna, Prague and Berlin. This update also corrects when defenders' hands open on misere.
confirmedMisereConvention: Only the talon is shown publicly before discard. The declarer's hand and discard remain private. Defenders open after the declarer's opening card, or before the opening lead if a defender leads.
